name: si.scriptura/scriptura
title: Scriptura
description: 1,254 great works and 12 Bible editions, original beside English, aligned by paragraph. No key.

tools.name: get_passage
tools.description: Read a Bible passage in one or more editions side by side (Hebrew WLC, Greek Septuagint, SBL Greek NT, English WEB/King James/ASV/Douay-Rheims/Brenton, Russian Synodal, Luther 1912, Louis Segond), each verse with its permanent link and a ready citation. Editions can be ids, short names or plain words ("kjv", "WEB", "Hebrew", "Greek"). Reference numbering is WEB, or WEB Classic for additional books it holds, otherwise Brenton. source_numbering identifies native verses. Unestablished correspondences are flagged aligned:false with no counterpart text. An unknown edition, a book an edition does not hold, or a verse range past the chapter's end is served as far as it can be and named in warnings[]; a verse or chapter that does not exist is an error with a hint.

editions.description: Editions, e.g. ["hebrew","lxx","kjv"] (ids from list_editions; a comma list works too). Defaults to the reference edition: en, web-full or lxx-en for that book.

tools.name: list_editions
tools.description: List the Bible editions available, with ids, languages and book coverage.

tools.name: who_read_verse
tools.description: Find who on the shelf (Church Fathers, rabbis, mystics, reformers, commentators, philosophers) quotes a given Bible verse, with the quotation and a link. So far only 42 well-known verses are indexed (Genesis 1:1, Psalm 23:1, Isaiah 53:5, John 1:1, John 3:16, Romans 1:17 ...); "indexed": false means the verse is not on that list, not that nobody quotes it.

tools.name: search_shelf
tools.description: Search the library by title, author, translator, blurb or group, also returning up to 20 matching section titles: Homer, Plato, Thucydides, Plutarch, Virgil, Livy and the rest of the Greek and Latin classics in the original beside English; the Pali Canon; Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Pushkin in Russian; Camus, Kafka, Goethe; Philo, Josephus, the Mishnah in Hebrew and English, 1-3 Enoch, Jubilees, the Church Fathers, Aquinas, Calvin, Kierkegaard, Nietzsche... To find a passage inside a work, use read_work with find.

group.description: Optional group filter, e.g. "Hidden books", "Rabbinic", "Church Fathers", "Commentaries"

tools.name: read_work
tools.description: Read a work from the shelf. Without a section: its table of contents (with paragraph counts). With a section: that section's text, original and translation row by row, up to ~24k characters; if truncated, call again with paragraph = next_paragraph to read on. With find: every row in the work (or in one section) containing all search words in any order, accent- and breathing-insensitive (e.g. find "αλοω κατα ποντον" or "worse than a brother"), with section and paragraph to read it. With find and mode "concordance": every occurrence of a word or phrase, in the original and the translation, each with the words around it, the same place in the other language and its link, 50 to a page. A section or paragraph the work does not have (or that is not a whole number) is an error that says how many it has; a section longer than one answer carries warnings[] beside next_paragraph.

id.description: The work: its id or address name from search_shelf (e.g. "plato-republic"), or a scriptura.si link.

paragraph.description: Start reading the section at this paragraph (1-based). Default 1.

find.description: Text to find inside the work, in any of its languages.

mode.description: "concordance" lists every occurrence of find, a page at a time. Default "find".

tools.name: room
tools.description: The Enoch and Melchizedek rooms: every passage on the shelf that names Enoch or Melchizedek, with links.

name.description: A room name, e.g. "enoch" or "melchizedek"; an unknown name returns the available names.

tools.name: follow_links
tools.description: Walk the shelf as a graph from a verse, a work or a room: which works quote a verse, which verses and rooms a work touches, which works a room names, and on again, as many steps as asked (default 1), with the quotation on every edge and a link to open it. Start from "John 1:1" (or "verse:JHN.1.1"), "work:<id>" or "room:<name>". Everything found is returned, in a fixed order; limit and offset are there only if you want to page. It follows the published index: the indexed verses and the Enoch and Melchizedek rooms, so a short answer is the edge of the index, not the edge of the library.

from.description: Start node: a verse like "JHN.1.1" or "John 1:1", "work:<shelf id>", or "room:enoch" / "room:melchizedek".

depth.description: How many steps to walk. Default 1.

limit.description: Optional: return this many edges at a time. Default: all of them.

offset.description: Optional: skip this many edges (use next_offset from the previous answer).

tools.name: cite
tools.description: Ready citations for a Bible verse or range, a work, a section or a paragraph: MLA 9, APA 7, Chicago 17, SBL 2 (Bible), BibTeX, RIS and CSL-JSON, with author, work, translator, Scriptura as the site, the permanent scriptura.si link and the access date, plus the quoted words. Stephanus or Bekker numbers appear where the text carries them. Takes a reference in any common form ("John 1:1", "Rep. 514a", a scriptura.si link) or a work with section and paragraph.

edition.description: Bible edition to cite, e.g. "kjv". Default: the reference edition.

id.description: The work: its id or address name from search_shelf (e.g. "plato-republic"), or a scriptura.si link.

paragraph.description: Paragraph, counted from 1 as read_work counts ("p-3", the page anchor, also works).

style.description: One or more of mla, apa, chicago, sbl, bibtex, ris, csl-json (comma list). Default: all.

tools.name: compare_translations
tools.description: Set one verse or range side by side in several Bible editions or languages (e.g. kjv, web, greek-nt, hebrew), aligned verse by verse, with a word-level summary of how two English editions differ; or one paragraph of a work in each of its languages (original, English, and a third language where there is one). Every row has its permanent link and citation.

ref.description: A Bible reference ("John 1:1", "PSA.23.1-3") or any reference resolve_ref reads.

editions.description: Bible editions or languages, e.g. ["kjv","web"] or ["hebrew","lxx","en"]; for a work, languages such as ["grc","en"]. Default: the original and two English editions.

id.description: The work: its id or address name from search_shelf (e.g. "plato-republic"), or a scriptura.si link.

paragraph.description: Paragraph, counted from 1 as read_work counts ("p-3", the page anchor, also works).

url.description: A scriptura.si link to a verse or paragraph.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: One paragraph of a work with the paragraphs around it (two each side by default), the section title and where it falls in the section; every paragraph in each of the work's languages, with its permanent link and citation. Useful after a find, a concordance hit or a reference, to read a quotation in its setting.

id.description: The work: its id or address name from search_shelf (e.g. "plato-republic"), or a scriptura.si link.

paragraph.description: Paragraph, counted from 1 as read_work counts ("p-3", the page anchor, also works).

tools.name: resolve_ref
tools.description: Turn a reference in any common form into Scriptura addresses and permanent links: Bible references ("Jn 1:1", "John 3:16 KJV", "Genesis 1:1 in Hebrew", "Jn 1:1 LXX"), Stephanus and Bekker numbers ("Rep. 514a", "Nicomachean Ethics 1094a"), book and line ("Iliad 1.1", "Aeneid 6.851"), sections ("plato-republic 7"), or scriptura.si links. Each address names the tool call that reads it; a reference that is not found comes back with suggestions.

tools.name: study
tools.description: Quiz questions (fill the gap, with choices) or flashcards made from one section of a work, each answer a sentence quoted from the text with its paragraph address and permanent link. A section gives the same items each time.

id.description: The work: its id or address name from search_shelf (e.g. "plato-republic"), or a scriptura.si link.

language.description: Which of the work's languages to draw on, e.g. "en" or "grc". Default English where the work has it.

tools.name: search_passages
tools.description: Find passages by the words inside them, across every Bible edition and every work, in every language (title-only search is search_shelf). Query: words, "an exact phrase", -leave out, author: work: group: lang: edition:. Returns results[] (work or edition, section, paragraph or verse, anchor, snippet with matches in « », the parallel text, url, cite), next_cursor, total_estimate, facets. Phrase hits rank above all-words above some; at most 2 per work. Example: {"query": "love your enemies", "scope": "bible"}. If empty: fewer words, no quotes, scope "all", or the word in the original language.

query.description: Words to find; "exact phrase", -exclude, author:plato, work:republic, group:"Church Fathers", lang:grc.

response_format.description: detailed adds the whole passage. Default "concise".

tools.name: check_quote
tools.description: Check a quotation before you quote scripture or a classic, or before you say who wrote it. Give the words in any language, with the author, work, Bible reference or edition they are said to come from if you know it. Scriptura looks for them in every text it holds, every Bible edition and every work on the shelf, in English, Hebrew, Greek, Latin, Russian, German, French, Pali and Chinese, ignoring accents, vowel points, punctuation and old spellings, and across verses and paragraphs. The answer gives the place, its permanent scriptura.si link, a ready citation (cite), the real wording, a word-by-word diff and the same passage in the other editions or the original language. status: exact (the words are there as given); near (the same words with small differences of spelling or wording); partial (part of the quotation, or a loose version of it, is there); ambiguous (the same words stand in several places, all listed); other_translation (the words are there, in another edition than the one named, shown beside it); misattributed (the words are there, but not by the author, in the work or at the reference named); not_found (the words are not in Scriptura's texts; that does not make them invented, since other translations and books exist; the nearest passages are listed); invalid (no words were given). The warning context_dropped means the quoted words leave out part of their sentence in a way that can change its sense.

text.description: The quotation, in any language (quote is accepted too).

claimed_author.description: Who it is attributed to, e.g. "Nietzsche" (author is accepted too).

claimed_work.description: The work it is said to come from, e.g. "Thus Spake Zarathustra" or "1 Timothy".

claimed_ref.description: A Bible reference it is said to be, e.g. "1 Timothy 6:10".

edition.description: The edition or translation it is quoted from, e.g. "kjv", "WEB", "NIV" or a translator's name.

lang.description: A language code to prefer, e.g. "en", "he", "grc", "la", "de".

tools.name: get_words
tools.description: The original-language words of a Bible verse, range or chapter, one by one: surface form, lemma, Strong's number, part of speech, parsing in words and codes, a one-word gloss, and the dataset behind each tag (Hebrew Bible: OSHB on the Westminster Leningrad Codex; Greek New Testament: MorphGNT on the SBLGNT). Automatic tags carry a confidence. Use it to read a verse word by word or to parse a form. Example: ref "John 1:1". If empty, check the book (the Septuagint is not tagged yet) or use get_passage for the text.

edition.description: "hebrew" or "greek-nt"; default is the book's own.

tools.name: lookup_lemma
tools.description: A dictionary entry for a Hebrew or Greek word given as a lemma, an inflected form, a Strong's number or a transliteration: lemma, Strong's number, part of speech, gloss, definition, how often it occurs in the Hebrew Bible or Greek New Testament, every verse it occurs in (page with offset and limit; default all), and example verses with links. Add "in" ("Genesis 1") to count and find it inside one book, chapter or passage. Example: q "H430" in "Genesis 1". If empty, try the Strong's number or the dictionary form.

q.description: Lemma, Strong's number or surface form: "H430", "G1510", "λόγος", "בראשית", "elohim".

offset.description: Skip this many occurrences in the list. Default 0.

limit.description: Occurrences to list. Default: all of them.

in.description: A book, chapter or verses to count within, e.g. "Genesis 1".

tools.name: open_reader
tools.description: Open Scriptura's reader inside the chat: the original beside the translation (or two Bible editions side by side), paragraph by paragraph, each with its permanent scriptura.si link. With nothing given it opens a short list of ways in. Give a work (slug or id, from search_shelf) with an optional section and paragraph (both 1-based, default section 1), or a Bible reference in any common form ("Jn 1:1", "Genesis 14:18-20", "JHN.3") with up to two editions ("kjv", "greek-nt", "hebrew", ids from list_editions). A scriptura.si address also works. The result lists the first page of paragraph pairs, each with url and cite; in hosts that render the reader, the person can turn pages and the paragraph they open is shared with you so you can quote it exactly. Cite every paragraph you use with its link.

work.description: A work slug or shelf id, e.g. "plato-republic".

section.description: Section of the work, or chapter of the Bible book. Default 1.

paragraph.description: Paragraph (1-based, as read_work counts) or verse to open at. Default: the first.

editions.description: Bible only: one or two edition ids, e.g. ["kjv","greek-nt"]; the first is the left column.

tools.name: reader_page
tools.description: For the reader app only: the next or previous page of paragraph pairs, or a jump to a section or chapter.

from.description: First paragraph or verse of the page; -1 for the last page of the section. Default 1.

tools.name: open_notebook
tools.description: Write a page of Markdown (headings, prose, lists, tables) in which every quotation is a reference, and Scriptura inserts the exact text: the model never types the quotation. Put {{Rep. 514a}}, {{John 1:1|grc,kjv}} (editions or languages after "|"), {{plato-republic/21#p-0}} or a scriptura.si link where a quotation goes, on its own line for a block (the original beside the English, with its verdict, citation and permanent link) or inside a sentence for a short inline quotation. Ordinary quotation blocks (> "…" — Plato, Republic) are checked against the texts and shown with the real wording. A reference that is not found shows plainly as "not found". In hosts that render apps it opens as a typeset page the person can expand, copy as Markdown, copy as a bibliography (MLA, Chicago, SBL, BibTeX) or print; in other hosts the result is the Markdown with the quotations filled in, each with its link and citation. Cite the quotations with the links the result lists.

markdown.description: The page, in Markdown, with quotations written as references: {{ref}} or {{ref|editions}}.

title.description: Optional title; the first heading is used otherwise.

tools.name: make_receipt
tools.description: Check a quotation against the text and make a card built to be screenshotted and shared: the claim (who said what), the words quoted, the real text at its place (the original beside the English), a verdict (exact, near, not in the text or misattributed) and the permanent scriptura.si link. Give the quote, the claim if there is one ("Nietzsche said …") and the place in ref if you know it ("John 1:1", "Rep. 514a"). It uses check_quote where Scriptura has it, otherwise resolve_ref and read_work with a plain comparison, and says which. In hosts without apps the result is the same receipt as plain text. The same receipt as a picture to post is at https://scriptura.si/api/receipt, with these arguments and format=svg.

claim.description: Who is said to have said it, e.g. "Plato said this about the cave".

ref.description: The place it is said to come from, e.g. "John 1:1" or "Rep. 514a".

tools.name: notebook_bibliography
tools.description: For the notebook app only: the citations of the quotations on the page in MLA, Chicago, SBL or BibTeX.

tools.name: lookup_word
tools.description: For the reader and notebook apps only: the lemma, morphology and gloss of a Greek, Hebrew or Latin word the person tapped. Answers only where Scriptura has word data.
